id: ml-03
title: Batch normalization
paper: Ioffe & Szegedy, Batch Normalization (arXiv Feb 2015; ICML 2015)
link: https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.03167
type: Mechanism
cutoff: 2015-02-11
domain: ml
profile: method-benchmark

## expected_verdict
Mixed (claim-level split). The performance claim is supported: faster training, higher learning rates, and ImageNet gains are widely reproduced. The mechanism claim, that BatchNorm works by reducing internal covariate shift, is contradicted. Santurkar et al. show BatchNorm still helps under injected covariate shift, and attribute the gain to a smoother loss landscape.

## I0
Does batch normalization improve training, and is reduced covariate shift the cause?

## evidence
- Method: normalize each layer's pre-activations per mini-batch, with learned scale γ and shift β; population statistics at inference.
- Mechanism claim (title, abstract): training is slowed by "internal covariate shift" (ICS); BatchNorm addresses it.
- Results: Inception with BatchNorm reaches the same accuracy in 14× fewer training steps; allows much higher learning rates; can remove the need for Dropout; ensemble reaches 4.9% top-5 validation (4.8% test) error on ImageNet.
- MNIST experiment showing more stable input distributions to a sigmoid layer with BatchNorm (evidence offered for ICS reduction).
- No experiment manipulates ICS independently of BatchNorm.

## intake
- Scope: two claims. (A) BatchNorm speeds and improves training of deep nets; (B) the mechanism is reduced internal covariate shift.
- Regime: CNNs (Inception) on ImageNet; MNIST MLP for the distribution plots.
- Assumptions: for (B), lower distribution drift of layer inputs causes the speedup.
- Falsifiers: for (B), BatchNorm still helps when ICS is deliberately increased, or ICS is not reduced by BatchNorm under a better ICS measure; for (A), no gain under matched learning-rate tuning.

## screen
- Must flag: the mechanism is asserted from correlational plots; performance and mechanism need different tests.
- Must request: an intervention that changes ICS while keeping normalization; a quantitative ICS definition.

## retrieval
- Pre-cutoff must-finds: covariate shift (Shimodaira 2000); input whitening (LeCun et al. 1998 efficient backprop); Glorot & Bengio initialization; Dropout (Srivastava et al. 2014); Inception / GoogLeNet.
- Current mode: Santurkar et al. 2018: VGG on CIFAR-10; injecting non-zero-mean, non-unit-variance noise after BatchNorm layers creates severe covariate shift, yet the BatchNorm network still trains well; BatchNorm improves Lipschitzness of loss and gradients (β-smoothness).

## designer
- Arms: no norm; BatchNorm; BatchNorm + injected noise (high ICS); alternative normalizers. Measure training speed at matched learning-rate sweeps, ICS metric, and gradient predictiveness.

## champion
- Same network without BatchNorm but with tuned learning rate and initialization; for mechanism, the noise-injected BatchNorm network.

## panel
- Accept claim A; flag claim B as unsupported by interventional evidence; recommend the noise-injection control.

## run
- CIFAR-10 VGG-11 with / without BatchNorm and with noise injection (Santurkar setup): small GPU job; check that noisy-BN still outperforms no-BN.

## verdict
- Label: Mixed: performance Supported (strong); ICS mechanism Refuted/contradicted.
- Must say: the method's benefit survives; its proposed explanation does not.
- Must not say: BatchNorm doesn't work; or the ICS explanation is established.

## audit
- Check: 14× fewer steps; 4.9% / 4.8% top-5; Santurkar noise-injection design and smoothness claim.

## variants
- Test alternative explanations (landscape smoothness, effective learning rate / scale invariance) with controlled interventions.
